title: 1950 AHSME Problem 27
statement: A car travels \(120\) miles from \(A\) to \(B\) at \(30\) miles per hour but returns the same distance at \(40\) miles per hour. The average speed for the round trip is closest to:

solutions.text:
The total distance is \(240\) miles. The travel times are \(4\) hours and \(3\) hours, so the average speed, in miles per hour, is \[ \frac{240}{4+3}=\frac{240}{7}\approx34.29 \] which is closest to \(34\) mph.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Average speed is total distance divided by total time
The two legs take \(\frac{120}{30}\) and \(\frac{120}{40}\) hours
